topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the course structure, themes, and specific learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Biological mechanisms and experimental modeling of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops through stepwise genetic and epigenetic alterations leading to disrupted differentiation and tissue architecture, and how these processes are studied using cell culture models.

topics.label: Pathology, progression, and nomenclature of benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define how benign and malignant neoplasms are distinguished by local tissue invasion and metastatic potential, illustrated through histological progression models and standard diagnostic nomenclature.

topics.label: Pathophysiological causes of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the specific physical, physiological, and metabolic mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors cause systemic disease and death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence across human populations and animal taxa
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of tumor incidence and mortality across human demographics, companion animals, and diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Cancer screening principles and organ-specific modalities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the clinical rationale for early tumor detection and compare specific screening approaches, diagnostic criteria, and outcomes across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical preview
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic wraps up the lecture by reiterating learning outcomes and looking ahead to upcoming practicals and future sessions.
